title: Cultural Expo
subtitle: Ten weeks, shown rather than written.
objectives: Recall the Music strand of the term
Recall the Arts strand of the term
Recall the PE strand of the term
Recall the Health strand of the term
Plan what to present at the expo

cards.title: Ten weeks, one table
cards.text: It is the term, shown rather than written. So the question is what each week gives you to show.

cards.title: Three weeks, three things to show
points: **Week 1:** play two notes and explain why one is higher.
**Week 2:** play a gangsa pattern toppaya, then palook.
**Week 3:** the same song through two formats.
**Show the mechanism**, not a poster of it.

cards.title: Ten weeks, what to show
cards.text: Tap each week. The second line is the trap that catches people.

options: two ways of striking a gangsa

cards.title: Three weeks, three things to show
cards.text: Each one is a made object.
points: **Week 4:** one subject in three periods' styles.
**Week 5:** a symbol you designed, with its meaning written.
**Week 6:** four panels in order, and the same four reordered.
**The reordered version** is the one people remember.

cards.title: An expo table is a user interface
cards.text: People walk past. You have about three seconds.
points: **One thing visible** from two metres away.
**One thing they can touch.**
**One sentence you say** before they ask.
**Everything else is detail** for whoever stays.

question.text: Which group takes about half the Pinggang Pinoy plate?

cards.title: Four weeks, two demonstrations
cards.text: These are the easiest to show and the most often turned into posters.
points: **Week 7:** run one game and name what it trains.
**Week 8:** lay out a real plate in the right proportions.
**Week 9:** run one fitness test on a visitor.
**Week 10:** show the plan, not only the finished video.

cards.title: Rehearse the sentence
cards.text: The one line you say when somebody stops at your table.
points: **Write it down.** Say it twenty times.
**Under fifteen words.**
**It names the thing and why it matters.**
**Then stop talking** and let them ask.

cards.title: The day itself is physical
cards.text: Standing and talking for two hours is harder than it sounds.
points: **Eat before**, not during.
**Water within reach.**
**Sit when nobody is at the table.**
**Talking all day will tire you** more than training does.

cards.title: The four strands
points: Music: what vibrates, how it is struck, how it reaches you.
Arts: periods, symbols, and the order of panels.
PE: what each game trains, and the five components.
Health: the plate, the proportions, and sleep.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 11 MAPEH, the term's showcase. The deck is built as a planning session rather than a revision list: each strand's card asks what that week gives him to demonstrate, and in every case the answer is a mechanism or a made object rather than a poster. The interactive review board doubles as the planning board, with the usual trap named for each week. The expo-table lens treats the table as an interface with a three-second budget, which is both true and the kind of concrete constraint that makes a vague task doable. The twenty-four question paper covers all four strands evenly.
discussion: Ask what he will show from each strand.
Ask him to say his one expo sentence out loud.
Ask which week has the weakest demonstration and what would fix it.
Ask what a visitor can touch at his table.
extension: Set up the table at home and have him run it for ten minutes.
Have him time his one sentence and cut it to fifteen words.
misconceptions: "An expo is a poster competition." Show the mechanism.
"More detail is better." One visible thing, one touchable thing, one sentence.
"Agility is a health component." It is skill-related.
